requirements.requirement: Restore branch_orders on node1 with supplied primary keys, customer/order relationships, and exact monetary values.
requirements.summary: The export was directly imported. Final schema inspection shows primary keys on both tables, the orders.customer_id foreign key, and DECIMAL(10,2); final rows exactly match the supplied IDs, relationships, and amounts, with zero orphan orders.

requirements.requirement: Provide a reporting account that can read orders and customers from node2 but cannot modify them.
requirements.summary: Remote joins and aggregate reads succeeded from node2. INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE were directly denied, and an UPDATE remained denied after both node restarts. Final privileges contain only SELECT on the two requested tables.
The administrator account has full branch_orders privileges, and transactional inserts from node2 succeeded before and after restart; both tests were rolled back and left no test row.
The final file retains its original 452-byte size, mode, timestamp, and SHA-256 hash, matching the preparation baseline and surviving node1 restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after evidence consistently shows RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. EL7 MariaDB 5.5.68 server/client packages operated successfully and recovered after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete on both nodes: healthy pre-restart states, acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and recovered service/data/access behavior are shown, with fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agreeing. Only minor cleanup and package-verification concerns remain.
limitations: Native package-health checks timed out before preparation, after preparation, and after execution on both nodes, so RPM dependency consistency was not independently confirmed despite successful installs and runtime behavior.
The final evidence did not re-audit repository configuration; earlier commands show the CentOS 7 vault repository enabled, with no later removal or disablement captured.
Requirement export_preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No state-changing command was clearly unrelated to the task: repository setup and package installation established prerequisites; database, firewall, account, and credential changes implemented the outcomes; transactional writes and reboots collected bounded evidence. Temporary credentials and the temporary SSH authorization were reverted or removed, and test writes were rolled back (cmd-31bbfe7b783844bc, cmd-fe6922db42ad42a5, cmd-ba9af73882534421). Hygiene is reduced by retained low-risk residue on both nodes: RPM key downloads, installer logs and stale PID files, and reboot logs remained under /tmp after execution. These originated from cmd-372f66d71b2d40c9/cmd-52a682175e214de4, cmd-71c8146fa5f743d7/cmd-f7fc5e26c61d4918, and cmd-2dbdc7fafb7b45ae/cmd-06f6c1d7aaa249d7, respectively. The enabled CentOS vault repository and imported key also remained; they enabled the required EL7 packages but leave a mixed-vendor update source. No failed services were observed, credentials were mode 600, and database exposure was restricted to node2.
